tasks.short: Estimate customer installation or production costs and savings from a proposed product.

steps.what: Discuss operating conditions, current costs, installation constraints and acceptable assumptions with the customer.
Retrieve equipment prices, installation rates, consumption figures and service costs.
Calculate installation costs, operating costs, savings and payback across customer scenarios.
Assess uncertain assumptions, omitted installation work and whether projected savings are credible.
Prepare a customer summary showing costs, savings, assumptions and exclusions.
Approve the estimate for release and explain its assumptions and tradeoffs to the customer.

tasks.design: A versioned calculator in the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines customer inputs from the {CRM} with prices from the {ERP} and approved technical parameters from the {DOCS}. It checks units and missing inputs, calculates scenarios, and generates an estimate summary in the {DOCS}; the sales representative approves its release and discusses uncertainty with the customer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Calculations were possible already, but customer baselines, supplier rates and local calculation templates were inconsistent. Maintaining links and tested formulas required scarce technical time.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce the effort to build input forms, connectors, calculation tests and templates. The calculation itself remains ordinary deterministic arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Installation conditions, production disruption and actual usage can dominate savings. A precise calculation cannot repair an unreliable baseline.
tasks.human_edge: Discover hidden operating constraints and explain which assumptions could change the buying decision.

ambition.what: A post-installation savings review comparing the original estimate with measured operating results.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding calculations to testing customer assumptions and discussing investment choices. Within delegated limits, the representative can choose which scenarios deserve a revised estimate; pricing authority does not automatically expand.

reach.task: Validate installation assumptions and operating performance ranges.
reach.learn: Unit consistency, equipment duty cycles, installation dependencies and sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: Cost and savings calculations can use deterministic calculators with human judgement over inputs and final assumptions.
Elfsquad links product configuration and quoting with finance and customer records; this supports adjacent infrastructure, not proof of savings accuracy.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one product family with agreed formulas and units.
Customer baselines are entered through structured fields; no model extraction is needed initially.
Access estimates include commercial data permissions and GDPR review where customer contacts are involved.
Build ranges cover an initial production scope, not every installation variant.
unknowns: Which calculation templates and assumptions are currently approved?
Which prices and installation rates are accessible through the {ERP}?
Who may approve estimates, exclusions and contractual savings claims?
Can customers provide reliable operating baselines and later performance measurements?
research_questions: Which published engineering methods apply to the chosen product family?
What independent benchmark cases can validate the calculator's results?
new_work: Maintain versioned formulas, rates and technical parameters.
Review missing inputs and implausible savings.
Compare estimates with actual costs and performance.
Retest calculations when product specifications change.

tasks.short: Help customers choose technically suitable products that meet their needs and applicable requirements.

steps.what: Discuss the application, operating environment, priorities and constraints with the customer.
Read technical specifications, application guidance and relevant requirements to identify selection constraints.

loop.input: Requirements brief and retrieved passages from approved, versioned technical and regulatory documents.
loop.output: Draft selection constraints with document versions, passage citations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for every constraint; flag conflicts and have the representative confirm applicability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per brief; missing evidence or conflicting requirements go to a sales engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Application conditions and exceptions appear in prose. Structured product attributes alone do not capture them.

steps.what: Check candidate products, valid configurations, availability and customer prices.
Prepare a comparison of suitable options, tradeoffs and outstanding technical questions.
Resolve uncertain compatibility, safety or regulatory questions for selections needing specialist input.
Approve the recommendation, explain tradeoffs and help the customer settle on a preferred option.
Record the preferred configuration, selection rationale and unresolved conditions.

tasks.design: Configure product rules in the {CRM}, linked to product, price and stock records in the {ERP}; generate comparisons from approved attributes. A bounded reader of the {DOCS} prepares cited constraints for review, while specialist exceptions and customer recommendations remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Configuration tools handled explicit rules, but application guidance and exceptions stayed in documents or specialist knowledge. Keeping technical content current was harder than filtering a catalogue.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding reduces the work of connecting records and generating comparison views. Bounded document extraction can prepare evidence without making the suitability decision.
tasks.still_hard: Suitability depends on the actual application, current standards and interactions between components. Encoded rules need technical ownership and validation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a customer's stated specification misses the real operating problem, and take responsibility for the recommendation.

ambition.what: Offer structured product-selection consultations to smaller customers previously served mainly through catalogue enquiries.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching manuals and more time discovering applications and explaining tradeoffs. They can handle a wider range of routine configurations within approved limits; specialist approval rights remain with the relevant technical role.

reach.task: Screen compatibility and application risks before preparing a technical solution.
reach.learn: Read specifications, distinguish certification from suitability, and identify escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad provides product configuration connected to quoting and business records.
Rules can filter valid configurations, while application assessment and final product choice require judgement.
Extracting cited constraints from prose is a plausible bounded model use; the digest provides no case proving regulatory-selection accuracy.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one product family and its approved application guidance.
Specialist review time is averaged across routine cases and cases needing escalation.
The {CRM} has configurable product-selection capabilities; otherwise that step requires deterministic development.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; product-specific requirements depend on the application.
Access work includes rights to use technical documents and customer application data.
unknowns: How complete and current are product attributes, configuration rules and technical documents?
Which selections require formal technical approval under existing policy?
Which product regulations and standards apply to the customer base?
Does the existing {CRM} support configuration rules and structured selection records?
research_questions: What authoritative sources and update mechanisms cover the relevant standards?
How reliably can cited constraint extraction handle the product family's exceptions and conflicting documents?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and resolve unsupported statements.
Maintain configuration rules and document versions.
Test known incompatible and borderline applications.
Track escalations and correct recurring gaps in product data.

tasks.short: Prepare customer-specific sales presentations and proposals explaining technical products and applications.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, application, buying criteria and proposal scope with relevant stakeholders.
Find approved specifications, application examples, diagrams, commercial terms and relevant estimates.
Adapt the narrative and assemble a presentation or proposal using approved templates.

loop.input: Proposal brief, approved source pack, template sections and permitted claims.
loop.output: Customer-specific narrative with source references, assembled into a proposal draft.
loop.check: Insert specifications, prices and terms deterministically; check narrative claims against sources and render the document for review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported claims are flagged and missing sections return to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout and facts, but explaining an application to different buying audiences needs tailored prose.

steps.what: Review the proposal's technical claims, customer fit, commercial commitments and final wording.
Send the approved proposal or presentation to the agreed customer contacts.
Attach the delivered version and update the opportunity's proposal status.

tasks.design: A generator combines a structured brief from the {CRM} with approved content and templates in the {DOCS}. Deterministic assembly inserts specifications, estimates and terms, while a bounded model drafts the application narrative; approval of the exact version and recipients releases delivery through the {EMAIL} and records it in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed, but representatives still searched for current material, tailored the story and copied facts between files. Content ownership and version control limited reliable reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes template assembly, source checks and record updates cheaper to build. A bounded drafting loop can adapt approved material to the customer's application.
tasks.still_hard: The proposal must reflect the real buying decision and avoid unsupported performance claims. Technical diagrams, unusual terms and multilingual layouts still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the argument that matters to the customer and recognise commitments hidden in seemingly harmless wording.

ambition.what: Provide an application-specific briefing for the customer's operations team alongside the purchasing proposal.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling documents to shaping the technical and commercial case. The representative gains control over audience-specific explanations within approved claims, without gaining authority to change contractual terms.

reach.task: Translate technical specifications into an application explanation for customer stakeholders.
reach.learn: Explain operating limits, evidence for performance claims and the technical implications of exclusions.

reach.task: Review whether a proposal addresses the buying committee's decision criteria.
reach.learn: Stakeholder mapping and concise commercial argument.

evidence.claim: ZARGES reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds using Elfsquad; this is a vendor case about quotes, not tailored presentations.
Approved content, deterministic document assembly and bounded narrative drafting can support proposal preparation.

assumptions: Approved content can be tagged by product, application, language and validity.
Commercial figures come from approved records rather than generated prose.
The proposal approval includes the exact recipient list, so delivery needs no separate approval interaction.
Preparation includes briefing and review discussions, but excludes delivering a live sales presentation.
Build ranges assume one proposal template and one presentation template initially.
unknowns: Who owns approved claims, diagrams, terms and translations?
Which proposal sections require specialist or commercial approval?
How many templates and languages must the first release support?
Can the {CRM}, {DOCS} and {EMAIL} exchange versioned documents and delivery status?
research_questions: Which document-generation approach best preserves the required editable layouts?
How well can factual checks detect unsupported claims across the required languages?
new_work: Review drafted narrative and document layout.
Retire outdated source material and maintain templates.
Handle missing diagrams, translations and unusual proposal terms.
Check that delivery always uses the approved version and recipients.

tasks.short: Complete expense claims, sales reports and routine sales administration.

steps.what: Enter expense details and attach receipts to a claim.
Check business purpose, cost allocation and required evidence, then submit the claim.
Approve the expense claim or return exceptions for correction.
Export sales records and copy order totals into a reporting workbook.
Reconcile totals, resolve discrepancies and prepare the periodic sales report.
Distribute the sales report to the agreed internal recipients.
Complete required visit and activity records, including outcomes and follow-up commitments.

tasks.design: Configure receipt capture, policy checks and approval routing in the {EXPENSE}, retaining employee certification and manager approval. A scheduled job in the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the {CRM} and {ERP}, publishes reconciled sales measures in the {BI}, and sends scheduled internal notices; structured forms in the {CRM} prefill routine activity fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing tools covered individual records, but reporting definitions, identifiers and approval routes differed between teams. Manual workbooks bridged the {CRM} and {ERP}.
tasks.enabler_now: Most of the change uses existing configuration and ordinary data integration. AI coding can reduce the effort to build mappings, reconciliation checks and report views.
tasks.still_hard: Revenue timing, returns, shared account ownership and expense exceptions need agreed definitions. A meeting date can be prefilled; its commercial outcome still needs the representative's account.
tasks.human_edge: Explain unusual expenditure and distinguish a meaningful customer commitment from a recorded activity.

ambition.what: Review stalled opportunities weekly using reconciled order and pipeline information.

tasks.altitude: The week loses much of its copying and report assembly, leaving exception review and customer follow-up. With delegated discretion, the representative can reprioritise follow-up using reconciled information; expense approval and revenue policy rights do not change.

reach.task: Use a reconciled pipeline review to identify stalled opportunities and agree next actions.
reach.learn: Pipeline definitions, data quality checks and the difference between activity and progress.

reach.task: Resolve mismatches between customer opportunities and booked orders.
reach.learn: Order identifiers, cancellations, returns and booking cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Expense configuration, structured activity records and scheduled reporting generally require no bespoke model loop.
The Netherlands requires works council consent for relevant employee-monitoring arrangements; other countries require assessment under national rules.
The digest provides no directly documented case for this combined expense and sales-reporting workflow.

assumptions: This is a blended administrative workload; step shares are provisional and include manager handoff time.
The {EXPENSE} supports receipt capture, transaction matching and configurable approval routing.
The future report reads source records directly, eliminating the intermediate reporting workbook.
Routine activity forms prefill metadata; representatives still enter substantive outcomes.
Consent and access ranges include GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it. Formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
The initial scope adds no call recording, transcription or employee scoring.
unknowns: What share of actual administration is expenses, reporting and activity paperwork?
Which receipt-capture and approval features are already available in the {EXPENSE}?
Do customer, opportunity and order identifiers match across the {CRM} and {ERP}?
Which reporting definitions and recipients are approved?
Which national rules, employee representation arrangements and access restrictions apply?
Would the reporting change introduce or materially change employee monitoring?
research_questions: What national consultation requirements apply to the proposed use of employee activity data?
Which deterministic reconciliation patterns best handle split orders, returns and shared accounts?
new_work: Review receipt mismatches and policy exceptions.
Maintain account mappings, report definitions and distribution permissions.
Resolve missing orders and conflicting ownership records.
Maintain approval routes when roles or cost centres change.
Review whether collected activity fields remain necessary.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward application discovery, technical judgement and customer investment discussions. Faster preparation supports broader customer coverage, while commercial commitments and specialist technical approvals remain within delegated authority.
reach: Sales engineer: qualify application constraints and interpret technical evidence.
Sales manager: use reconciled pipeline information to choose follow-up priorities.
Order clerk: resolve opportunity-to-order mismatches before they distort customer discussions.
skills_to_grow: Clear explanation of assumptions and exclusions
Review of generated proposals and cited constraints
role.ambitious_version: Become an application adviser who connects product choice, investment estimates and post-installation results, using repeatable tools to make that service viable for smaller customers.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
